options: Mixins generate CSS, functions return values
Functions generate CSS, mixins return values
explanation: Mixins output CSS rules directly; functions compute and return values for use in properties.
SCSS variables have block scope; $color is only available inside .parent block, so .sibling reference causes an undefined error.
@extend couples selectors tightly; changes to .base affect .derived unexpectedly; mixins provide explicit reuse without coupling.
@each iterates over map entries; #{} interpolates variable names into selectors, generating separate rules for each color.
& represents the parent selector; &:hover becomes button:hover, &::before becomes button::before.
Preprocessor @import merges all imports into a single compiled CSS file; browser import() is different (creates HTTP requests).
Each nested level adds a selector to the compiled rule; deep nesting creates overly specific selectors (0,0,3,1) that are hard to override.
Preprocessor functions run at compile time; $base-size * 1.5 = 24px is computed and inlined into CSS.
CSS custom properties are runtime-mutable (in media queries, JS); preprocessor variables are compile-time only.
